To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the intensive preparatory training in L1 essay writing for university exams influenced the L2 essay writing of Japanese university students.

(1) intensive training in essay writing in L1 and L 2 has an influence on task response and text construction in the L1 and L1, and (2) the interaction between intensive training in L1 essay writing and intensive training in L2 essay writing has an influence on how students perceive L1 writing and L2 writing.

(1) intensive L1 training for university entrance exam essays promoted a sense that L1 essay writing is different from L2 essay writing, (2) intensive L2 training for university entrance exams promoted a sense that the L1 and L 2 essay writing are the same, and (3) the interaction between intensive training in L1 essay writing and L2 essay-writing promoted a sense that both L1 and L1 essay writing are the some.
In summary, our research is concerned with

how the intensive training in L1 essay writing for university exams influences the students’ L2 essay writing, and the results suggest the need for more empirical studies on the transferability of writing skills across L1 and L2.
the effects of intensive training on students’ task response and text construction in L1 and L 2 writing.

how students perceive the nature and characteristics of L1 and/or intensive L2 training and how these perceptions influence the way in which they approach the task of writing in their first and second languages.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the intensive L1 writing training and the L2 training both contributed to the students’ development as writers, but the L2 training had a more profound effect on the development of their writing competence than the L1 training.
the intensive L1 training in essay writing had the greatest impact on the task response, and that the intensive L2 training had the greatest effect on the text construction.

the intensive preparatory training in L1 writing has a positive effect on students’ L1 writing, and the intensive preparatory L2 writing training has a positive effect, but only in the case where the training focuses on the structure of essays, on students’ L2 writing.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the intensive L1 and/or intensive L2 writing training in high school had a significant influence on the students’ writing performance in L1 and L 2 at university level, and the effects of the training were found to be transferable across L1 and/orL2.
intensive preparatory training in L1 essay writing for university exams has a significant influence on the students' writing in both L1 and L 2.
the L2 writing training, in addition to L1 training, can enhance the L2 writing performance, and the L1 writing training, in conjunction with L2 training, can promote L1 and L 2 writing performance.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the students’ writing competence was not simply a matter of language proficiency but was shaped by the interaction between the writing training they received in L1 and in L2, as well as the students’ own perceptions of L1 and/or of L2 writing.

the effects of intensive training on L1 and L1 writing can differ depending on the type of writing training received, the language of the training, and students’ perceptions of the similarities and differences between L1 and L 2 writing.
the intensive training in L1 writing can have an impact on L2 writing, and vice versa.
